Device Battery Status **1.0.0** is the official stable Windows x64 release for personal use. Both packages are **unsigned**.

Changes in this release:

- Implemented Razer HyperPolling battery and native product/link discovery, shared mouse/keyboard routing, and association checks around battery and charging reads. Added 18 documented mouse paths and three additional receiver masters. Unknown products require explicit role evidence; ambiguous replies cannot become another peripheral's battery.
- Extended Razer manual polling to associated mouse identities, preserving the documented ordinary/high-rate profiles, explicit Apply, per-phase authorization and readback. Receiver rate profiles do not establish a peripheral's negotiated capabilities or measured USB timing.
- Added 13 Logitech receiver IDs, including Bolt and Nano, with fresh slot/unit association. Native categories remain categories; no estimated percentages are introduced. Supported direct-percentage alternatives are queried when their capabilities permit them.
- Removed the unnecessary HID++ feature-version-zero restriction. Added a separate opt-in to switch Logitech onboard-profile mice to software mode on Apply, then revalidate identity and available rates. This may change active DPI/button behavior; profile memory is not edited.
- Preserved genuine zero, original stale sample times and separate current/disconnected/unsupported/failed states. A receiver being plugged in does not prove its peripheral is connected.

Choose **self-contained** for the bundled .NET/Windows Desktop runtime, or **framework-dependent** if .NET 10 Windows Desktop Runtime x64 is already installed. Extract the complete application ZIP and keep its files together. Sibling SHA-256 assets and the verification ZIP record package integrity, source provenance and automated test evidence.

Compilation, automated software tests and static package inspection are separate from application runtime and physical hardware verification. Runtime, hardware compatibility, firmware caching/sample age, physical polling measurements and performance work are saved in the [deferred verification record](https://github.com/kA-sp3R/BatteryStatusCheck/blob/main/docs/deferred-verification.md) at the user's request. Deferral does not establish a passing result or hardware certification. Protocol bounds remain explicit in the [support documentation](https://github.com/kA-sp3R/BatteryStatusCheck/blob/main/README.md); unknown device capabilities are never invented. Alienware Pro retains its AWCC-derived implementation and documented lack of a unique headset serial.

Software verification for source `c2c5d747a0952da7e34826d1cfdd117f7f93bd52`:

- [Windows compilation and package build](https://github.com/kA-sp3R/BatteryStatusCheck/actions/runs/39679709333): both ZIP flavors passed static archive, payload hash, x64 GUI PE, runtime and license-provenance inspection; no application launch. Downloaded packages independently matched their embedded source/run manifests and every payload hash.
- [Full Windows software suite](https://github.com/kA-sp3R/BatteryStatusCheck/actions/runs/39679716090): **779 C# tests passed in Debug and 779 in Release**, with zero failures or skips; **5 parser tests** and **11 release-policy tests** passed.
- The verification ZIP contains the exact source/run manifest, full TRX reports and logs. Runtime and physical hardware were not exercised.
